registry_name: Platform B1 Agentic & Ambient AI Vendor Assurance Passport Registry
passport_name: Agentic & Ambient AI Vendor Assurance Passport™
purpose: Define a stronger-than-checklist assurance passport for evaluating agentic AI, ambient AI, AI documentation, AI copilots, and vendor-operated AI systems before and after deployment in regulated healthcare, pharma, laboratory, and manufacturing contexts.
core_question: Can this AI-supported vendor system, documentation output, recommendation, agentic action, or workflow be trusted, reconstructed, reviewed, governed, and defended at the moment it matters?

positioning.not_just_checklist: This is not merely a vendor checklist. It is a pre-contract, pre-deployment, runtime, and audit-reconstruction assurance passport.
positioning.platform_a_relationship: Platform A captures use case intent, vendor role, intended use, risk class, authority model, human review design, evidence requirements, data boundaries, and lifecycle governance design.
positioning.platform_b1_relationship: Platform B1 evaluates whether evidence, authority, review, accountability, vendor controls, lifecycle controls, and action admissibility are sufficient.
positioning.thread_d2_relationship: Thread D2 / RAMAT Vision displays assurance state only. It does not approve, release, diagnose, treat, or override source systems.

source_problem_statement: Agentic and ambient AI systems may be deployed before governance documentation is mature.
AI-generated documentation may be clinically or operationally influential even when humans remain accountable.
A signed or approved output is not defensible unless the organization can reconstruct what the AI produced, what the human saw, what changed, who approved it, and what authority applied.
Human-in-the-loop is not sufficient unless the human identity, qualification, review time, authority, evidence, and final accountability are provable.
Information governance is part of AI governance because AI behavior depends on governed information boundaries, provenance, purpose, retention, access, and release controls.

assurance_domains.assurance_question: What is the AI system intended to do, what decision or workflow can it influence, and what consequence could follow?
red_flags: system can influence consequential action without classification
organization treats all AI outputs as low risk

assurance_domains.assurance_question: Which regulatory, quality, privacy, safety, and contractual obligations apply to this AI use case?
red_flags: vendor says compliance is entirely customer responsibility
no documented mapping to applicable controls
regulated use is hidden under productivity language

assurance_domains.domain_name: Data, Privacy, Consent, and Information Governance
assurance_domains.assurance_question: What information does the AI access, capture, generate, retain, disclose, transform, or destroy?
red_flags: unclear whether customer data trains vendor models
no source provenance or data lineage controls

assurance_domains.assurance_question: Can the vendor and its subprocessors be trusted contractually, operationally, and evidentially?
red_flags: no clear data return or deletion procedure

assurance_domains.domain_name: Model, Agent, Tool, and Automation Boundary
assurance_domains.assurance_question: What can the AI model, agent, or tool call actually do, and where are its execution boundaries?
red_flags: agent can execute actions without governed authority

assurance_domains.assurance_question: Who is the accountable human or role, what authority do they have, and what happens if they are silent, unavailable, or unqualified?
Can the organization reconstruct what was captured, what the AI generated, what the human saw, what changed, who approved it, and when?
red_flags: no proof of what reviewer saw
AI draft and final record cannot be compared

assurance_domains.assurance_question: How was the AI system tested before use, and how is performance verified in real operating conditions?
red_flags: vendor relies only on generic accuracy claims
no test of realistic workflow conditions

assurance_domains.assurance_question: Are identity, access, privilege, session control, and logging sufficient for regulated AI use?
red_flags: logs cannot identify the human or agent actor

assurance_domains.domain_name: Change Control, Drift, and Lifecycle Monitoring
assurance_domains.assurance_question: How are model, prompt, workflow, configuration, and vendor changes governed over time?
red_flags: vendor can change model behavior without notice

assurance_domains.domain_name: Incident, Deviation, CAPA, Complaint, and Safety Readiness
assurance_domains.assurance_question: What happens when the AI output is wrong, unsafe, misleading, incomplete, biased, or operationally harmful?
red_flags: no incident route for AI-generated errors
vendor support does not preserve evidence

assurance_domains.domain_name: Exit, Continuity, Data Return, and Decommissioning
assurance_domains.assurance_question: Can the organization safely exit, pause, replace, or decommission the AI system without losing evidence or continuity?
red_flags: business process becomes dependent on unverifiable AI service

required_outputs: MODEL AND AGENT BOUNDARY REVIEW REQUIRED

assurance_scoring_model.critical_domain_failure_rule: Failure in human authority, evidence reconstruction, data governance, security logging, or incident readiness creates ACTION NOT ADMISSIBLE WITHOUT EVIDENCE regardless of total score.

boundary: No Platform B1 local validation bundle count change.
No real LIS, MES, ERP, eQMS, QMS, VRS, EPCIS, pharmacy, EHR, or radiopharma production data.
